chunks: Ali ibn Ahmad narrated to us, from Ubaydillah ibn Musa al-Alawi, who said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Qalanisi told me in Mecca in the year 267 AH, saying: We were narrated by Ali ibn al-Hasan, from al-Abbas ibn Aamir, from Musa ibn Hilal, from Abdullah ibn Atta al-Makki, who said:

I set out for Hajj from Wasit, and I visited Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali (peace be upon him). He asked me about the people and the prices (in the market). I said: 'I left the people stretching their necks towards you; if you rise (to power), the people will follow you.' He said: 'O Ibn Atta, you have spread your ears to the fools! By Allah, I am not your master, and none of us who is pointed at with fingers and towards whom eyebrows are stretched (in expectation) will die except as a martyr or by his own death (natural death). I said: 'And what is 'his own death' (hatf anfih)?' He said: 'He dies of anger in his bed, until Allah sends one whose birth is not emphasized (unknown/obscure).' I said: 'And who is the one whose birth is not emphasized?' He said: 'Look for the one whom the people do not know whether he was born or not; that is your master.'

key_terms.حَتْفَ أَنْفِهِ: Death by natural causes (as opposed to martyrdom)

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Baqir say about the nature of the Mahdi's birth and visibility?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Nu'mani’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights the transition from the visible Imamate of the Ahl al-Bayt to the occultation of the Mahdi, emphasizing that the true leader will emerge from obscurity rather than political prominence. The Imam’s description of dying 'from suppressed anger' (*khatf anfah*) reflects the historical reality of the Imams' martyrdoms under Umayyad and Abbasid surveillance, while the phrase 'one whose birth is not known' (*man la yu'bah lahu bi-wiladatihi*) serves as a key eschatological indicator for the Hidden Imam's identity.
